newsitem.title: USA: American, pilots to talk through weekend.
newsitem.headline: American, pilots to talk through weekend.

text.p: Contract talks between American Airlines and its pilots are expected to continue through the weekend, the two sides said on Friday.
Representatives of American, a unit of AMR Corp, and Allied Pilots Association met on Friday to resume talks for the first time in four weeks.
The union said it had no indication whether any progress had been made in the session.
"Talks are expected to continue throughout the weekend at the discretion of Robert Harris," a union spokesman said.

Harris is the head of the Presidential Emergency Board (PEB), formed by the White House on February 15, shortly after pilots went on strike to resolve a contract dispute with the second-largest U.S. airline.

Clinton's decision to convene the board forced the American's 9,300 pilots to return to work for 60 days. During the first 30 days, the board was to gather information from both sides and make proposals for a contract settlement.
After any proposals from the board, the pilots have 30 days to decide whether to accept a settlement.

If the pilots reject the recommendations, they are free to strike. Congress, however, can pass legislation to force the pilots to return to work and accept the board's proposal or force them into binding arbitration with the airline.
APA President James Sovich earlier in the week said the union and American would try to reach an agreement before the the board submitted its report to President Clinton on March 17.
The talks could extend into next week if the board opts to delay submitting its report to the president, the union said.
